title: plain oRTB imp signals popunder via ext.adtype, bid ships a window.open script

source.name: ortbtools Core pop-family ext-hint recognition contract (packages/core/non-iab-formats.js STRING_HINT_KEYS, packages/core/rules/pop-request/index.js, packages/core/rules/pop-response/index.js) layered on IAB OpenRTB 2.x Imp/ext extensibility — the product's own documented, in-repo mechanism for pop/clickunder signalling, not a named vendor's wire format
source.version: repo HEAD at session start, commit a61fc25
source.license: Internal product code (ortbtools); no third-party material copied. MIT for the original fixture values.
source.notes: This case exercises the plain `iab` dialect plus Core's baseline non-IAB format scanner, deliberately without loading the `ext-rtb` vendor dialect — the pop-request/pop-response rule plugins and non-iab-formats.js hint scanner run unconditionally regardless of dialect selection.

modifications: All IDs, domains, prices and timestamps independently authored.
device.ip uses TEST-NET 192.0.2.44; user.id is a clearly synthetic string.
advertiser.example.test / tracking.example.test / publisher.example.test are reserved .test hosts; no live host, tracker or subscriber identifier.
provenance.sanitized: No real visitor or subscriber data. IP 192.0.2.44 is TEST-NET-1; every identifier is a synthetic-fixture string; every URL uses a reserved .test hostname.

pairApplicability.note: A genuine oRTB auction pair: the response bid references the offered impression, ids match, and the ext hint is a Core-recognized, non-vendor-attributed extension convention, not a proprietary wire wrapper.

device.ua: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

specNotes: packages/core/non-iab-formats.js STRING_HINT_KEYS recognizes imp.ext.adtype='popunder' as a pop hint at any of the scanned ext locations; the finding is imp.non_standard_format (INFO) at rules-request.js:527, oRTB 2.6 §3.2.4 Object:Imp extensibility.

packages/core/rules/pop-response/index.js's own header comment documents exactly three accepted pop adm shapes: a bare landing URL, a `<script>window.open(URL)</script>` blob, or a location/top.location redirect. A `window.open(...)` script is the first of the two script shapes — admLooksLikePop must accept it and bid.pop.adm_not_redirect must not fire.

packages/core/crosscheck.js's pop-landing rule (3d-pop) extracts the window.open destination host and compares it against bid.adomain; a matching adomain must produce crosscheck.bid.pop.adomain_landing_match (OK), never the mismatch CRIT.

A minimal 1x1 banner object keeps the impression a spec-valid oRTB Imp (at least one of banner/video/native/audio present, oRTB 2.6 §3.2.4) alongside the pop ext hint — this is not itself a claim that the ad renders as a 1x1 banner.

Browser preview must not open a real popup or dispatch tracking; the script executes inside a sandboxed iframe with no allow-popups permission, so window.open() is inert by the sandbox itself, not by the tool refusing to render it.
notes: This is the plain `iab` dialect, not the `ext-rtb` vendor dialect used by the sibling EXADS/Kadam/PPCmate/Adon3 pop cases — the mechanism under test (non-iab-formats.js hint scanning, pop-request/pop-response plugins, the 3d-pop crosscheck rule) runs unconditionally regardless of which dialect is loaded.

preview.limitation: pop script has no visual body

knownGap.note: The redirect-script pop is detected and an inert destination note is built, but it does not reach the measured on-screen identity: the caption is appended beside a zero-footprint iframe and the harness still reads no visible marker. The sandbox refusal itself is correct and unchanged.
